title: The Marquee Self-Portrait: Florida Street, the Plaster Cast, and the Shoe That Was Also Sculpture
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Lecce, the Glass, and the Two Birth Years

stops.name: Lecce, the parents leave Apulia
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no emigration year, port, or ship is recorded anywhere; 1935 is a placeholder inside the pre-war decade
stops.campa: From Lecce in Apulia a family named Puzzovio takes ship for the Rio de la Plata, joining the migration that gives Buenos Aires half its surnames. No manifest, no year, no port of embarkation survives in any reachable source; only the Spanish Wikipedia line calling her the daughter of Italians from Lecce. The English edition never mentions the city and files her under Argentines of Italian descent instead. No source at any point places Dalila herself in Italy. Lecce stands on this map as the point of departure she inherits, not a street she walks.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (hija de italianos oriundos de Lecce)
English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (Category:Argentine people of Italian descent, no Lecce)
suggested_refs: Italian emigration registers for Lecce province, unconsulted in this pass

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the birth two editions claim
stops.date_confidence: contested: English Wikipedia and Wikidata Q5797644 give 1943, Spanish Wikipedia gives 1945 uniformly across infobox, lead and persondata; no day or month is recorded in any source, and the 1 January is a year-precision placeholder, not a record
stops.campa: Dalila Puzzovio is born in Buenos Aires, and the record splits at the first line. English Wikipedia and Wikidata write 1943; Spanish Wikipedia writes 1945 in its infobox, its opening sentence, and its persondata alike. No hospital is named, no neighbourhood, no day, no month. The atlas that will later pin her to a dozen exact street doors cannot fix the first of them. Getty ULAN follows the English reading and prints 1943. She enters the century two years wide, and every age given for her in this file is given twice.
suggested_refs: Argentine civil registry for the City of Buenos Aires, 1943 and 1945, unconsulted

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the girl who draws on the window glass
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: English Wikipedia dates the parental encouragement to about age twelve and cites nothing; her own account of what she drew on is undated recollection given in 2009
stops.campa: The parents encourage the drawing, and the girl works on whatever surface the house offers. She draws on the window glass. She cuts stamps out of erasers. She takes ink to the wallpaper of her own bedroom and alters it. English Wikipedia dates the encouragement to about age twelve and cites nothing for it; the account of what she actually did comes from her own mouth, more than forty years later, to a newspaper in Santa Fe. None of the three surfaces is made to be drawn on. No work from these years is recorded in any reachable source.
stops.quote: Me la pasaba dibujando los vidrios de la casa, inventaba sellos con la goma de borrar, con tinta modificaba el empapelado de mi cuarto...
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio, interviewed by Georgina Lacube, 'La reina del pop', El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, 15 August 2009
sources: Georgina Lacube, El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, 15 August 2009
suggested_refs: The full Lacube interview text, ellitoral.com, 15 August 2009

stops.name: Buenos Aires, an apprenticeship no document records
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: English Wikipedia states plainly that no documentation of formal education exists, and supplies the 1961 endpoint itself; Spanish Wikipedia gives the two names with no dates at all
stops.campa: She studies, the sources say, with the surrealist Juan Batlle Planas and with Jaime Davidovich, until 1961. English Wikipedia states in the same breath that no documentation of formal education exists, which turns the whole apprenticeship into tradition; Spanish Wikipedia gives the two names and no dates. Davidovich was born in 1936 and leaves for New York in 1963, an unlikely master for a woman seven years his junior. No studio address survives for either man. A decade earlier this same city held Cesar Milstein and Ernesto Guevara as students, and the atlas finds no evidence they met either.
suggested_refs: Any surviving enrolment or atelier record for Juan Batlle Planas, unlocated

segments.name: Lirolay: the Debut and the Shells

stops.name: Galeria Lirolay, the first exhibition
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year and venue by both Wikipedia editions; no month is recorded, and the coordinates are Nominatim's geocode of Esmeralda 868, Retiro, the gallery's address until its 1969 move to Paraguay 794
stops.campa: At Esmeralda 868 in Retiro, in a small commercial gallery Mario and Paulette Fano opened the year before, Puzzovio holds her first exhibition. Lirolay shows the artists the museums will not, and it will stay open until 1981. She is eighteen by one birth year and sixteen by the other. Nothing of what hung on the walls is recorded in any reachable source, only that the show happened and where. It is the first address in her life that can be pinned, four years ahead of the institute on Florida.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Galeria Lirolay' (Esmeralda 868; founded 1960 by Mario and Paulette Fano; closed 1981)
suggested_refs: The Lirolay exhibition ledgers, 1960-1981, unlocated in this pass

stops.name: Buenos Aires, meeting Charlie Squirru
stops.date_confidence: attested as the year they met by both Wikipedia editions; no marriage date, church, or registry appears in either edition or in Wikidata, which carries only the bare spouse statement
stops.campa: She meets Carlos Squirru, called Charlie, a painter of the same pop generation. Every source agrees on the year and on what follows: a working partnership of decades, furniture and shoes designed together, a billboard shared, his black and acid humour supplying the titles for her sculpture. Wikidata records him as her spouse and gives no date. Neither Wikipedia edition names a wedding year, a church, or a registry office. The marriage is attested as a fact and nowhere as an event, so the atlas can pin the meeting and not the vow.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (a quien conocio en 1962)
English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (whom she had met in 1962)
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires civil marriage registry, 1960s, unconsulted

stops.name: Galeria Lirolay, the show Germaine Derbecq curates
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, venue and curator by Spanish Wikipedia; English Wikipedia dates a Derbecq collaboration to 1963 but attaches it to the plaster casts and names no venue
stops.campa: She returns to Esmeralda 868 for a show curated by Germaine Derbecq, the French painter and critic who came to Buenos Aires as the wife of the sculptor Pablo Curatella Manes and stayed on. Spanish Wikipedia gives her dates as 1899 to 1973 and names her as the curator, dating the show 1963. English Wikipedia records a Derbecq collaboration in 1963 too, but attaches it to the orthopedic casts and names no room. The two editions are describing either one event or two, and neither says which.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (curada por la artista francesa Germaine Derbecq, 1899-1973)
suggested_refs: Germaine Derbecq's Lirolay curatorial papers, unlocated

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the orthopedic workshops and the shells
stops.date_confidence: attested as to material and title by both editions; the year is English Wikipedia's, and Spanish Wikipedia dates the exhibition of this body of work to 1964 instead
stops.campa: She goes to the orthopedic workshops and takes away what they throw out: plaster casts cut off healed limbs, hollow, still holding the shape of a body that has walked away. She calls the results Cascaras, shells. The material is a documentary record of suffering and she works against its grain, giving it a hedonistic side and letting Charlie Squirru title the pieces in his acid register. The empty cast is her signature before she has a public, and she will still be casting thirty-five years from here.
sources: Felisa Pinto, 'Bienes gananciales', Pagina/12, Las12, 9 May 2008
suggested_refs: Surviving Cascaras casts in Argentine museum holdings, uncatalogued in this pass

stops.name: Museo de Arte Moderno, Cascaras in the San Martin complex
stops.date_confidence: contested: Spanish Wikipedia dates Cascaras to 1964 at the Museo de Arte Moderno, curated by Rafael Squirru; English Wikipedia dates the same body of work to 1963, credits Germaine Derbecq, and names no venue
stops.campa: Cascaras is shown at the Museo de Arte Moderno, then housed inside the Teatro General San Martin complex on Corrientes, curated by Rafael Squirru. So Spanish Wikipedia, which dates it 1964. English Wikipedia puts the same body of work a year earlier and in Germaine Derbecq's hands, naming no room at all. The atlas carries both readings and adjudicates neither. What is not in dispute is the object standing in the museum: plaster cast on living bodies, cut away when they healed, kept when it was meant to be thrown out.
stops.quote: Hice esa suerte de esculturas con un material torturado y documental del sufrimiento, pero traté de que tuvieran un costado hedonista y apelé al humor negro, irónico y ácido de Charlie para poner los títulos de las obras.
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio to Felisa Pinto, 'Bienes gananciales', Pagina/12, suplemento Las12, 9 May 2008
suggested_refs: Museo de Arte Moderno de Buenos Aires exhibition records for 1963-1964

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, the nucleus around Romero Brest
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date: Spanish Wikipedia attests her membership of the Romero Brest nucleus but gives no year for it, and the span 1965-1970 used elsewhere is the institute's general peak, not a documented span for Puzzovio
stops.campa: Florida 936. The Centro de Artes Visuales of the Instituto Torcuato Di Tella, run by the critic Jorge Romero Brest, gathers the nucleus that Spanish Wikipedia lists by name: Antonio Berni, Jorge de la Vega, Juan Carlos Distefano, Leon Ferrari, Gyula Kosice, Alberto Greco, Delia Cancela, Pablo Mesejean, Julio Le Parc, Marta Minujin, Luis Wells, Federico Peralta Ramos, and Puzzovio. No source dates her entry into it. Ten of the thirteen names on that list are men's, and the list itself is the only evidence that she belonged to the nucleus at all.
suggested_refs: The Instituto Torcuato Di Tella Centro de Artes Visuales archive, Universidad Torcuato Di Tella

stops.name: Walker Art Center, New Art of Argentina
stops.date_confidence: attested as a catalogue appearance by English Wikipedia, citing the Walker Art Center and Instituto Torcuato Di Tella exhibition catalogue; whether she personally travelled to Minneapolis is confirmed by no reachable source
stops.campa: Thirty Argentine artists are chosen for New Art of Argentina, mounted jointly by the Walker Art Center and the Instituto Di Tella, and Puzzovio is among them. The catalogue is issued jointly in Minneapolis and Buenos Aires, and it is the earliest printing of her name in English that this pass could reach. Whether she crosses the equator to stand at the Minneapolis opening is confirmed by nothing reachable here. The catalogue travels; the traveler may not have.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio', citing Walker Art Center and Instituto Torcuato Di Tella, New Art of Argentina (1964)
suggested_refs: Walker Art Center registrar files and opening-night records, New Art of Argentina, 1964

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, the exhibition comes home
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the Buenos Aires leg of the exhibition by English Wikipedia; no month is recorded and the June is a placeholder
stops.campa: The exhibition comes home to Florida 936, and the argument it was built to make is made on the artists' own ground: that what is happening in Buenos Aires is contemporary with New York and London, not derivative of them. Puzzovio is twenty-one by one reckoning and nineteen by the other. English Wikipedia records the Buenos Aires leg and gives no month, so the pin sits on a placeholder June. The institute's address and the corner she will rent as a billboard a year from now stand on the same street.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires press coverage of New Art of Argentina at Di Tella, 1964

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the crowns for non-human inhabitants begin
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the 1964 start and the 1998 end by English Wikipedia, which gives the span without months or exhibition history
stops.campa: She begins the series she will still be making thirty-four years from now: Coronas para los habitantes no humanos, crowns for the non-human inhabitants, cast in white and in black. English Wikipedia gives the span 1964 to 1998 and says the casts evoke mortality. Nothing else about the series appears in any reachable source: no venue, no count, no catalogue, no word on who the non-human inhabitants are. It runs underneath the loud decade and keeps running for twenty-eight years after that decade ends.
suggested_refs: Any exhibition record for Coronas para los habitantes no humanos, 1964-1998, unlocated

stops.name: Florida y Viamonte, the billboard
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, corner, three participants and wording by both Wikipedia editions; no month is recorded and no photographic facsimile was reached in this pass
stops.campa: At the corner of Florida and Viamonte, in the retail spine of the city, Puzzovio, Charlie Squirru and Edgardo Gimenez rent a hoarding and put their own three faces on it under a question. It sells nothing. It advertises them, in the exact grammar of commercial advertising, as famous before they are famous. Both Wikipedia editions print the line identically. The English gloss that circulates with it is wrong: son is third person plural, so the poster asks about neither you nor us but about them, three strangers on a wall.
stops.quote_source: Text of the 1965 billboard at Florida y Viamonte, Buenos Aires, as printed in Spanish Wikipedia and cited by English Wikipedia to Marina Alejandra Wabnik, 'Identidad Grafica Argentina', 2011, p. 35
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio', citing Wabnik (2011), p. 35
suggested_refs: A photographic facsimile of the Florida y Viamonte hoarding, 1965; fate of the boards unrecorded

stops.name: New York, the trip recorded in a subordinate clause
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: Spanish Wikipedia records the trip with no year, month, itinerary or venue, footnoting it to Pagina/12 and La Nacion; 1965 is a placeholder inside the mid-1960s
stops.campa: Spanish Wikipedia records, in a subordinate clause, that she travelled to New York with Squirru, and footnotes it to Pagina/12 and La Nacion. That is the whole of it. No year, no gallery, no address, no month, no reason given. It is the only stop on her record outside Argentina and Peru, and the one this atlas can say least about. The city where Jaime Davidovich, named as her teacher, emigrated in 1963 receives her at some point in the same decade, and no source puts the two of them in a room.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (con quien viajo a Nueva York), footnoted to Pagina/12, Las12, 9 May 2008 and La Nacion nota_id=1004617
suggested_refs: The La Nacion piece, nota_id=1004617, not opened directly in this pass

stops.name: Buenos Aires, dressing Help Valentino
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year by both Wikipedia editions; neither names the theatre, and no month is recorded
stops.campa: She dresses Help Valentino, a cabaret revue. Both Wikipedia editions date it 1966, both name the show, and neither names the theatre it played in. The costume work starts here and runs nineteen years, through musical comedy, film and television, until 1985. It begins in the same year as the Di Tella self-portrait and the prize that came with it. The city giving her prizes for sculpture is also paying her to clothe comedians, and she treats the two commissions as one practice: the object is made to be worn in public and judged there.
suggested_refs: Buenos Aires theatre programmes for Help Valentino, 1966; venue unidentified

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, Autorretrato en marquesina
stops.date_confidence: contested: English Wikipedia dates the work 1966-1967, Spanish Wikipedia dates it by its prize year, 1966; the atlas takes the earlier bound and flags the range
stops.campa: She has cinema billboard painters, artisans of the marquee, execute a canvas over two metres by three and a half. It shows the body of the international model Veruschka lying on sand in a jewelled bikini, and the model's face has been replaced by Puzzovio's own. Spanish Wikipedia titles it Autorretrato en marquesina, self-portrait on a marquee, which names the technique and the joke together. In these same years Jorge Luis Borges is writing in this city and Victoria Ocampo publishing in it; the atlas tracks all three across one decade and records no meeting.
stops.quote: Cuando veo esta obra hoy, aquí, me doy cuenta de que esa apropiación todavía resiste al tiempo, y no como suele suceder en esta nueva moda de formato, ser como comida congelada. Mi autorretrato, creo, se puede volver a mostrar sin que nadie se intoxique.
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio to Felisa Pinto, 'Bienes gananciales', Pagina/12, suplemento Las12, 9 May 2008
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio', citing Maria Jose Herrera, Pop! La consagracion de la primavera (Fundacion OSDE, 2010), pp. 25-26
suggested_refs: Herrera, Pop! La consagracion de la primavera (2010), pp. 25-26, read only at second hand through English Wikipedia

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, the prize and the taxi
stops.date_confidence: contested: Spanish Wikipedia's prose calls it the Gran Premio Nacional 1966, its own awards list on the same page calls it the second Premio Nacional Di Tella, and English Wikipedia calls it her first Premio Nacional without a year; no month is recorded
stops.campa: The Instituto Di Tella gives her a national prize for the self-portrait, and the sources cannot agree what rank it carried. Spanish Wikipedia's prose says grand prize; its own list of honours, further down the same page, says second prize; English Wikipedia says first, and gives no year. What survives intact is the arrival. She gets out of the taxi at the ceremony in double-platform shoes, a satin miniskirt and a monkey-fur jacket, and two policemen look at her and decide against it.
stops.quote: The day we went to the Di Tella award ceremony, I got out of the taxi wearing platform shoes, a satin miniskirt, and a monkey-fur jacket, and two policemen didn't know whether to grab me or what; they looked at me with such fear that they let me pass by, they just weren't up for it.
stops.quote_source: Quoted in Laura Podalsky, Specular City: Transforming Culture, Consumption, and Space in Buenos Aires, 1955-1973 (Temple University Press, 2004), p. 142; read here only as reproduced with citation in English Wikipedia
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (prose and awards list, mutually contradictory)
Podalsky, Specular City (2004), p. 142, at second hand
suggested_refs: Podalsky, Specular City, p. 142, not opened directly; book unreachable in this pass

stops.name: Lima, the biennial prize
stops.date_confidence: attested as an award by Spanish Wikipedia's list alone; English Wikipedia never mentions Peru, the venue within Lima and her personal attendance are unrecorded, and the coordinates are the city centroid used as a placeholder
stops.campa: The Bienal de Lima gives her a prize. Spanish Wikipedia's awards list carries the line and English Wikipedia never mentions Peru at all. No venue, no work named, no ceremony, no evidence that she crosses the Andes to collect it. In the same season, down the same coast, Cecilia Vicuna is making her first Precario on a Chilean beach and starting the magazine Tribu No. Two Southern Cone women invent a discardable art in the same two years, in two capitals, and no source records either knowing the other's name.
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1966, Premio Bienal de Lima, Peru)
suggested_refs: Bienal de Lima 1966 catalogue and prize list, unlocated

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, forty pairs in glass cubicles
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, count and format by English Wikipedia; Spanish Wikipedia records the double-platform shoe with no year at all, and the 1965 date given for the Squirru furniture-and-shoe collaboration in earlier passes is unsupported by either edition
stops.campa: Forty pairs of women's platform shoes, made double, stand in glass cubicles at the institute. They are not sculptures of shoes. They are shoes, and they will be sold. From the vitrine they move to the display window of a commercial retailer, and the distance between an object shown and an object bought, which this whole decade has been testing, closes to nothing. She has been designing shoes and furniture with Squirru for years by now, though no source will say from which year.
stops.quote: Creo que las grandes afirmaciones necesitan grandes manifestaciones, aquí sí la idea fue convertir la obra de arte en una experiencia de consumo.
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio to Georgina Lacube, 'La reina del pop', El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, 15 August 2009
suggested_refs: Surviving pairs of Dalila Doble Plataforma in museum or private holdings

stops.name: Grimoldi, Florida Street, the work goes on sale
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: English Wikipedia names Grimoldi as the retailer but confirms no branch, and the Florida Street placement is inferred from the firm's period presence on that street; the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: Grimoldi, an established Buenos Aires shoe firm, carries the Dalila Doble Plataforma. Which branch is not recorded, and the atlas puts the pin on Florida because that is where the city kept its shoe windows. A woman who has never once entered the Instituto Di Tella can buy the work and walk out wearing it. Two blocks along the same street, at number 936, the institute is treating the identical object as sculpture. Neither edition records a price, a run, or how many of the forty pairs were sold.
suggested_refs: Grimoldi company records and 1967 press advertising, unconsulted

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, the second prize nobody can classify
stops.date_confidence: contested: Spanish Wikipedia's awards list gives 1967, second Premio Internacional Di Tella; English Wikipedia gives a second Premio Nacional in 1968, resting the claim on a reference its own article renders as an unpublished student practical assignment; no month is recorded
stops.campa: A second Di Tella prize follows, and it is the most confused entry in her record. Spanish Wikipedia's list dates it 1967 and calls it the second international prize. English Wikipedia dates it 1968, calls it a second national prize, and rests the whole claim on a reference the article itself prints as a final practical assignment, which is to say a student exercise. The atlas states both and prefers neither. Her own memory of a Di Tella prize keeps none of the confusion.
stops.quote: ¡Absolutamente exultante! No sólo por el premio, sino también por la posibilidad de concretar el sueño de la obra realizada tal como la había imaginado.
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio to Georgina Lacube, 'La reina del pop', El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, 15 August 2009
sources: Spanish Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1967, 2. Premio Internacional Di Tella)
English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (second Premio Nacional, 1968, citing 'TRABAJO PRACTICO FINAL')
suggested_refs: Instituto Di Tella prize records, 1966-1968, which would settle rank and category

stops.name: Buenos Aires, dressing Libertad Leblanc for Psexoanalisis
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, actress, film and director by English Wikipedia; no month is recorded
stops.campa: She dresses Libertad Leblanc for Psexoanalisis, directed by Hector Olivera. It is film work, on a named title, for the actress the Argentine screen of the period builds its scandal around. English Wikipedia names the year, the star, the film and the director, and gives that same precision to every costume job that follows. The record is thin about her sculpture and exact about her clothes, which is the reverse of what the prizes would predict. Nothing of the costumes themselves survives in any reachable source.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1968, costumes for Mrs. Libertad Leblanc for the film Psexoanalisis directed by Hector Olivera)
suggested_refs: Psexoanalisis (1968) production credits and surviving costume stills

stops.name: Teatro Comico, costumes for Malvina Pastorino in Pepsi
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, production, star and venue by English Wikipedia; the coordinates are Av. Corrientes 1280, address of the Teatro Comico, later renamed Teatro Lola Membrives
stops.campa: Costumes for Malvina Pastorino in Pepsi, at the Teatro Comico on Corrientes. The pop decade is finished as a scene, and Puzzovio moves onto the street where Buenos Aires keeps its theatres and stays there fifteen years. The billboard artist is now dressing the people who stand under the marquee lights she once had painters imitate on canvas. Nothing about the transition is recorded as a decision; it appears in the sources only as a list of jobs with years attached to them.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1969, costumes for Mrs. Malvina Pastorino, Pepsi, Comic Theater, Buenos Aires)
suggested_refs: Programmes for Pepsi, Teatro Comico, Buenos Aires, 1969

stops.name: Teatro General San Martin, costumes and set for La Vera Historia de Salome
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, production, credit and venue by English Wikipedia; the coordinates are Nominatim's geocode of Av. Corrientes 1530
stops.campa: Costumes and set design both, for Miguel A. Rondano's musical comedy La Vera Historia de Salome at the Teatro General San Martin. It is the same municipal complex on Corrientes that housed the Museo de Arte Moderno when Cascaras was shown there seven years earlier. She has exhibited inside this building and now she furnishes its stage. English Wikipedia records the double credit, costumes and set together, which no other engagement in the list carries.
suggested_refs: Teatro General San Martin production archive, 1971 season

stops.name: Teatro Estrellas, costume for Hello Tato
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, production, star and venue by English Wikipedia; the theatre's street address was not independently verifiable and the coordinates are an explicit Corrientes district placeholder
stops.campa: Costume for Hello Tato, the musical comedy carried by Tato Bores, at the Teatro Estrellas. Bores is the comedian the country watches to hear what cannot be said plainly, and the year is 1975, the last one before the coup. The atlas cannot find this theatre's street number in any reachable source and pins it to the Corrientes district as a stand-in, which is an honest placeholder and not an address. She is thirty by one birth year and thirty-two by the other, and the city is a year from the coup.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1975, costume for the musical comedy performed by Tato Bores, Hello Tato, Teatro Estrellas)
suggested_refs: Street address of the Teatro Estrellas, Buenos Aires, unlocated in this pass

stops.name: Buenos Aires, costumes for Con sabor a Pinky
stops.date_confidence: attested by English Wikipedia, which gives the span 1977-78 without months or a studio
stops.campa: Costumes for Con sabor a Pinky, a television show, across two years. Television is the last medium she has not dressed, and she reaches it in the first full year of the dictatorship. Nothing in any reachable source connects her work to the politics of those years in either direction: no exile, no signature on anything, no denunciation, no state commission. The record simply continues, one production per line, through a period when a great many Argentine records stop mid-page.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1977-78, costumes for the television show Con sabor a Pinky)
suggested_refs: Argentine television archives for Con sabor a Pinky, 1977-1978

stops.name: Hotel Bauen, costumes for the Maria Creuza show
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, performer and venue by English Wikipedia; the coordinates are Nominatim's geocode of Hotel Bauen, Av. Callao 360, Balvanera
stops.campa: Costumes for the Maria Creuza show at the Hotel Bauen on Callao, a Brazilian singer in a modernist hotel that will outlive its owners. Twenty years on, after the collapse of 2001, this building is taken over and run by its own workers as a recuperated enterprise. In this same year Isabel Peron leaves Buenos Aires for exile, the atlas's other traveler on the 1981 page of this city. One of them is dressing a singer on Callao; the other is going out of the country for good.
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Dalila Puzzovio' (1981, costumes for the Maria Creuza show, Hotel Bauen)
suggested_refs: Hotel Bauen programme records, 1981; cooperative archive after 2001

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the fashion period closes
stops.date_confidence: attested as an endpoint by English Wikipedia, which states that until 1985 she focused on developing herself as a fashion designer by making costumes for film and theater; no month or occasion is given
stops.campa: English Wikipedia closes the fashion period at 1985: until then, it says, she developed herself as a fashion designer by making costumes for film and theatre. Nineteen years of it, from Help Valentino to here, and the sources give no reason for the ending any more than they gave one for the beginning. She is in her forties by either birth year. The plaster casts of the sixties are two decades behind her, and the series they started, the crowns for non-human inhabitants, is still running.
suggested_refs: Any interview or catalogue essay explaining the 1985 turn, unlocated

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the magazine years
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: English Wikipedia gives no start date and closes the magazine work at the beginning of the 1990s, placing only the interior and architectural advice across the 1980s and 1990s; 1986 is a placeholder
stops.campa: She writes, edits and illustrates for popular magazines, Vogue among them, and advises on interiors and architecture. English Wikipedia closes the magazine work at the start of the 1990s and never says which Vogue: an international edition, a licensed local title, or freelance pages sold wherever they would take them. It is the least documented decade of her life and the one in which she is most steadily employed. Her own account of the period turns on continuity rather than on change.
stops.quote: En el trabajo de hoy (arte, arquitectura o moda), aunque parezca que cambié, sobreviene siempre sin excepción una tozudez que yo llamo estilo.
stops.quote_source: Dalila Puzzovio to Georgina Lacube, 'La reina del pop', El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, 15 August 2009, speaking of her work at that date
suggested_refs: Vogue mastheads and contributor lists, Argentine and international editions, 1980s

stops.name: Museo de la Ciudad, the prize for the best recycled house
stops.date_confidence: attested as to year, prize name and awarding institution by Spanish Wikipedia's awards list; no month, no address of the house, and no jury record
stops.campa: The Museo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires gives her its prize for the best recycled house. Spanish Wikipedia's awards list names it exactly. It is not a fine art prize but an architecture and interiors prize, and it is the only entry in her record that puts a finished building behind the design work of these years. No address for the house appears in any source. The woman who made sculpture out of discarded plaster casts is now decorated for reusing a house.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the crowns stop
stops.date_confidence: attested as an endpoint by English Wikipedia, which gives the span 1964-1998; no month, no final exhibition, no closing catalogue
stops.campa: The crowns for non-human inhabitants stop. English Wikipedia gives 1998 as the end of the series it began in 1964, which makes it thirty-four years long, longer than the entire Di Tella era it grew out of. What the last crown looked like, where it was shown, whether anyone noticed the series close: none of it is recorded in any source reachable here. It ends the way it ran, without a catalogue, and the plaster that had held the shape of departed bodies is set down.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, Hibridos and the screen
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the 1998 start and the medium by English Wikipedia; no month is recorded and the June is a placeholder placing the new series after the old one closes
stops.campa: In the same year she moves to digital photographic collage and calls the series Hibridos. The plaster cast held the shape of a body that had left; the composite photograph holds bodies that were never in one place at all. She is doing again, on a screen, what she had cinema billboard painters do by hand in 1966, setting one person's face on another person's body. No studio address, no exhibition history and no image list for the series appears in any source reachable here.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the El Litoral interview
stops.date_confidence: attested: the interview is published in El Litoral, Revista Nosotros, on 15 August 2009, and the page was read in full in this pass
stops.campa: A newspaper in Santa Fe sends Georgina Lacube to interview her, and the page it prints on 15 August 2009 is the richest document in her file: the childhood, the shoes, the sixties, the prizes, all in her own sentences. It is the only source in this pass that is not an encyclopaedia entry or a footnote to one, and the only place where she says what she takes herself to have been. The headline the paper puts on her is la reina del pop, a phrase she uses of herself nowhere in the interview.
stops.quote: Se puede decir que fui revolucionaria en las imágenes e ilusionista con los materiales.

stops.name: La Rural, El Deslumbre at arteBA
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to venue: English Wikipedia's only citation for El Deslumbre is an arteBA page headed Proyecto Dalila Puzzovio / Patio Bullrich, which does not confirm the La Rural pavilions; the year, the fair and the content are attested
stops.campa: At arteBA she rebuilds the shoe-store window of 1967 as an installation, calls it El Deslumbre, the dazzling, and lets the public walk a catwalk through it. Forty-four years on, the gesture that collapsed gallery into shop is staged inside an art fair, which is both at once. The pavilion is an inference: the only citation behind the piece points at a Patio Bullrich project rather than at La Rural, and the atlas marks this pin provisional instead of pretending to a floor plan.
stops.quote: Vistos ya desde el siglo XXI, estos años han pasado como una ceremonia excéntrica que parecieron perfectamente naturales...

stops.date_confidence: attested as to year by Spanish Wikipedia, citing a Legislatura de la Ciudad Autonoma de Buenos Aires statement; Wikidata carries the honour without any date, and no month is recorded
stops.campa: The city legislature, in its building on Peru near the Plaza de Mayo, declares her a Personalidad Destacada de la Cultura. Spanish Wikipedia dates it 2019 and cites the legislature's own statement; Wikidata carries the honour with no date at all. It is the last dated entry in a list that opens with a contested national prize in 1966, and it comes from the municipality rather than from a museum: the city claiming the woman who once rented its advertising space to announce herself.

stops.name: Instituto Di Tella, the work enters the archive
stops.date_confidence: attested as a holding by English Wikipedia, undated; the 2020 is a placeholder for an ongoing institutional fact, not an accession date
stops.campa: Her work enters the permanent holdings of the Centro de Artes Visuales del Instituto Di Tella. The room is an archive now, and the address outlives the scene. The family philanthropy that funded it also stands behind the Universidad Torcuato Di Tella, where the atlas's Javier Milei will begin and abandon a postgraduate degree, the only other Di Tella anywhere in this corpus. Same name, same money, two generations apart, and nothing else shared but a surname on a facade.

stops.name: Museo de Arte Moderno, San Juan 350
stops.date_confidence: attested as a holding by English Wikipedia, undated; Wikidata separately names the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes, and neither list was checked against the museums' own catalogues in this pass
stops.campa: Her work is also held by the Museo de Arte Moderno, now at San Juan 350 in San Telmo, not the Corrientes rooms where Cascaras was shown in 1964. Wikidata adds the Museo Nacional de Bellas Artes; English Wikipedia does not, and neither list was checked against a museum catalogue here. The critic Graciela Melgarejo is cited as crediting her with opening a road that later Argentine artists took. Which artists, the source does not say, and the atlas does not guess.

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the traveler with no grave
stops.date_confidence: attested by absence: no death date appears in English Wikipedia, Spanish Wikipedia, Wikidata Q5797644, or Getty ULAN, and English Wikipedia states that she currently works and resides in Buenos Aires
stops.campa: She is alive, in Buenos Aires, and there is nothing to visit. No tomb, no plaque, no monument, no plot. The atlas keeps its own cemetery at Recoleta, where Eva Peron lies among the traveling dead of every other journey, and Puzzovio is the traveler that ground does not hold. Nor does any file in this corpus name her: not Borges, not Charly Garcia, a schoolboy in this same city in 1967 while she is selling shoes as sculpture on Florida. Every crossing on this map is a shared street and a shared year, said out loud as such.
